title: Code Generation
explain: For a model or coding agent that writes, edits or fixes code, the main signal is execution: run it. Layer the checks from cheap to expensive: static (compile, type-check, lint, security scan), dynamic (hidden tests and the existing suite), diff (scope and compatibility), semantic (does it meet the real requirement?) and honesty (did it run what it says it ran?). Tests prove only the behaviours they exercise. (跑起来比看起来重要.)
model:
| Layer | Evidence | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Static | parse, compile, type-check, lint, SAST, dependency scan | required checks pass, no new high-severity issue |
| Dynamic | hidden unit/integration/e2e tests, property-based, existing suite | target behaviour passes; no regression |
| Diff | review of changed files | no unrelated refactors, API compatible |
| Semantic | acceptance checklist, human or judge | every requirement covered |
| Agentic / honesty | trace of commands, claims vs diff | no claimed-but-unrun verification |

**Metric:** `pass@k` = chance at least one of `k` samples passes; unbiased from `n` samples with `c` passing: `1 - C(n-c, k) / C(n, k)`. Report pass@1 for one-shot products.

**Slices:** feature, bug fix, refactor, migration, test generation; single-file to repository-level; clear, ambiguous or wrong specs; strong, weak or missing tests; concurrency, error handling, security-sensitive code.

**Gate:** correctness, regression, scope and security pass *independently*; flaky or environment failures labelled apart from model failures. Text metrics (BLEU, exact match) are not primary. Compare [tool-using agents](#/sd/f/eval-tool-agent).

details.q: Why not BLEU or exact match against a reference solution?
details.a: Many different programs are correct, and a small textual change (`<` versus `<=`) can break correctness while keeping high text similarity. Execution against tests measures behaviour; use text metrics only as weak diagnostics.

With `n` = 10 samples of which `c` = 3 pass, pass@5 = 1 - C(7,5)/C(10,5) = 1 - 21/252 = 0.92, while pass@1 = 0.3. A big gap means the product needs a verifier or more samples; it does not mean single-shot quality is high.

details.q: The tests pass, but are the solutions right?
details.a: Tests prove only what they exercise. If 80 of 100 pass but a reviewer finds 12 of those hard-code outputs or special-case visible inputs, at most 68% are genuinely correct. Add hidden and property-based tests, mutation tests and diff review to catch overfitting.

details.q: How do flaky tests distort scores?
details.a: With 100 independent tests each failing spuriously 1% of the time on a correct solution, the chance of at least one false failure is 1 - 0.99^100 = 63.4%. Rerun failures, quarantine flaky tests, and attribute environment failures separately from model failures.

details.q: A patch fixes a one-line off-by-one but reformats 14 files and renames two public functions. Pass?
details.a: Fail on scope discipline and API compatibility: the independent gates mean a green test run does not offset an over-broad diff. Reviewers need a minimal change, and renames can break callers the visible tests do not cover.

details.q: What do you check for security?
details.a: Run SAST and dependency scanning on the diff, add targeted tests for injection, authorization and secret handling, and have expert review on sensitive areas. Gate on no newly introduced high-severity finding, separately from functional correctness.

details.q: Order the checks from cheap to expensive.
details.a: Parse and compile, then type-check, lint and security scan, then unit and regression tests, then integration and end-to-end in a sandbox, then human or judge review of the diff. Fail fast on the cheap deterministic ones; reserve review for candidates that already pass.

points: Chance at least one of k samples passes
A gap to pass@1 means you need a verifier or more samples
